beats.subline: Tuesday, September 15, 2026 close — stocks fell for a second straight session as Treasury yields hit their highest level since 2007 ahead of the Fed's decision.
beats.body: Chip and AI-linked names extended their slide as the 10-year Treasury yield climbed to its highest level since 2007 and oil stayed elevated on Middle East supply worries, with investors bracing for the Fed's Wednesday rate decision.

beats.headline: House passes Iran war powers resolution for a third time, with a record seven Republicans in support
beats.body: The House voted 220-204 on Tuesday to advance a Democratic-led resolution directing President Trump to end US military operations against Iran absent explicit congressional authorization; seven Republicans -- Thomas Massie, Brian Fitzpatrick, Warren Davidson, Tom Barrett, Mariannette Miller-Meeks, Zach Nunn and Nancy Mace -- crossed party lines, up from four on the last such vote. Like its predecessors, the resolution does not carry the force of law.

beats.headline: Taiwan tracks 15 PLA aircraft sorties and 8 PLA Navy ships in latest 24-hour count
beats.body: Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense detected 15 PLA aircraft sorties, eight PLA Navy vessels and two official ships operating around the island in the 24 hours to 6 a.m. Wednesday local time, with 12 of the sorties crossing the median line into Taiwan's northern, southwestern and eastern air defense zones as Beijing keeps up pressure ahead of Xi Jinping's September 24 Washington summit.

beats.headline: Pentagon inspector general puts Iran war cost at $33.4 billion and warns of a munitions shortfall
beats.body: The Defense Department's first inspector general report on Operation Epic Fury tallies $33.4 billion in costs through June 30 -- two-thirds of it expended munitions -- and says the pace of use has caused 'strategic inventory shortfalls' and exposed industrial-base bottlenecks; the report also documents hundreds of damaged or destroyed buildings, dozens of destroyed aircraft and more than 400 US servicemembers wounded.

beats.headline: Air Force secretary confirms for the first time that the US has weapons stationed in space
beats.body: Air Force Secretary Troy Meink told the Air, Space and Cyber Conference the US has fielded 'on-orbit space control weapons capable of defending the Joint Force against hostile adversary action' -- the first official US confirmation of space-based weapons -- without disclosing what they are, tied to the broader Golden Dome missile-defense buildup and years of concern that China and Russia are developing their own counterspace capabilities.

beats.headline: Novo Nordisk partners with Anthropic to put Claude Science to work on drug discovery
beats.body: Novo Nordisk announced it will evaluate Anthropic's newly unveiled Claude Science models in select R&D workflows, aiming to accelerate drug discovery through AI-assisted biological reasoning and agentic software engineering under defined data-governance and human-oversight rules. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said growing AI capability could compress 'a century's worth of biological and medical breakthroughs into a decade,' as Claude Science joins similar pushes into pharma R&D from Google and OpenAI.
